column3: With respect to the St. Louis Portfolio Mortgage Loan (9.2%), the borrower sponsor disclosed that he served as CEO of a network testing and security products company from 2012 to 2013, when he departed following an internal investigation. The SEC subsequently alleged that he directed improper revenue recognition practices in violation of GAAP and signed SEC filings he knew to be false. The borrower sponsor resolved the matter, without admitting or denying the allegations, by consenting to a five-year officer/director bar and paying a $100,000 civil penalty. Related shareholder class actions filed in 2013 were settled, with preliminary court approval granted in 2016.
